sib.t: Latham & Watkins Legal Engineering Attorney and Legal Workflow Engineer Roles
The emergence of the 'legal engineer' role (job postings and commentary, 2025-2026)

dom.t: Reliable delivery: Legal engineering bridges capability and service

st.t: Reliable delivery: Legal engineering bridges capability and service
st.an: The source operationalises the cluster’s multidisciplinary implementation theme by specifying a legal-engineering role that combines workflow design, generative and agentic AI, systems integration, governance, change management and cross-functional collaboration. It adds concrete evidence of employer demand for these capabilities, while providing no measured evidence of reliability, productivity or service outcomes.

st.t: Legal engineering: Implementation extends beyond prompting
st.an: Halliburton’s posting directly supports the proposition that legal engineering is a dedicated, cross-functional implementation role extending beyond prompting. Its remit covers workflow translation and automation, AI-agent deployment, phased adoption and training, output verification and governance, and performance measurement. It specifies intended responsibilities rather than demonstrating achieved gains.

mo.t: AI hiring: Implementation demand meets recruitment uncertainty
Buyer transformation: Legal departments may capture AI gains
Human oversight: Accountability is not effective control
Legal workflows: Immediate gains create competence risks
Operating model: AI shifts bargaining across providers

kp.k: Legal engineering anchors an AI-enabled in-house legal function
kp.d: Halliburton describes an intended legal operating model centered on automation, with a Legal Engineer designing and deploying technology within its Legal Automation, Operations, and Risk Management team and reporting to that team's senior director. The posting expresses organizational aims for faster, higher-quality services at scale rather than reporting measured results.
qs: Halliburton’s Law Department is shaping a modern, AI-enabled legal function that invests in automation to deliver fast, high-quality legal services, decisions, and outcomes at scale.
The Legal Engineer sits at the center of that effort, designing and deploying technology solutions that make the department's workflows faster, smarter, and more scalable.
This role sits within the Legal Automation, Operations, and Risk Management team and reports to the Sr. Director, Legal Automation, Operations, and Risk Management

kp.k: Automation responsibilities extend across legal and compliance workflows
kp.d: The described role combines workflow analysis with practical implementation, including building AI agents for contracts, intake, matter management, regulatory processes, litigation support, eDiscovery and knowledge management. Reduced cycle times, lower risk and improved work quality are stated objectives, not demonstrated outcomes.
qs: Partner with attorneys, legal and compliance professionals, and business stakeholders to understand their workflows, identify opportunities for automation and improvement, and develop solutions that reduce cycle times, minimize risk, and improve work quality
Translate legal and business requirements into practical, repeatable technology solutions

Design, configure, and implement AI-powered and automated solutions across the full range of legal and compliance workflows, including building AI agents, and spanning use cases such as contract management and review, legal intake and matter management, compliance and regulatory processes, litigation support and eDiscovery, and knowledge management, among others

kp.k: Deployment includes change management and continuing professional training
kp.d: Halliburton assigns the Legal Engineer responsibility for readiness assessments, phased deployment and post-launch review across teams and geographies. Training, practical guidance and ongoing skill-building are part of implementation, while proven ability to drive adoption among legal professionals is a hiring requirement.
qs: Lead programmatic rollout of innovative technology solutions, including stakeholder readiness assessments, phased deployment plans, and post-launch reviews to ensure consistent adoption across teams and geographies
Design and deliver training programs, practical guides, and ongoing skill-building initiatives that equip legal professionals to use legal technology and AI tools effectively and responsibly
Proven change management skills, with a track record of driving adoption of new tools and processes among legal professionals

kp.k: AI governance encompasses output validation and regulatory compliance
kp.d: The role supports responsible AI practices, output validation protocols and compliance with evolving regulations and company policies. Experience with AI governance is preferred. The document does not specify validation procedures or the degree of human supervision for AI agents.
qs: Contribute to AI governance for the Law Department, including supporting the development of responsible AI practices, output validation protocols, and compliance with evolving AI-related regulations and Company policies
Experience with AI governance frameworks, responsible AI principles, or compliance with emerging AI regulations

kp.k: Technology investment is to be assessed through operational metrics
kp.d: Halliburton requires piloting emerging tools and tracking efficiency, accuracy, adoption and cost savings to demonstrate return on investment and guide future priorities. These are prospective measurement responsibilities; the posting supplies no achieved savings, accuracy figures or other performance results.
qs: Evaluate and pilot emerging legal technology and AI tools. Bring forward recommendations for continuous improvement

Establish and track performance metrics for deployed solutions, including process efficiency gains, accuracy improvements, user adoption rates, and cost savings, to demonstrate return on investment and inform future priorities

kp.k: Qualifications combine legal operations expertise with applied AI skills
kp.d: The role requires a bachelor's degree and a minimum of 2+ years of combined experience in legal technology, legal operations, process automation or a related discipline; a JD is strongly preferred rather than required. Prompt engineering and practical generative and agentic AI proficiency are required, while integration and scripting knowledge sufficient to extend existing tools is preferred.
qs: Bachelor's degree required. Juris Doctor (JD) strongly preferred
Minimum of 2+ years of combined experience in legal technology, legal operations, process automation, or a related discipline
Proficiency in prompt engineering and the practical application of generative and agentic AI tools in legal workflows

Working knowledge of APIs/MCPs, system integration concepts, or scripting languages (e.g., Python) sufficient to configure workflows, connect platforms, and extend the capabilities of existing AI and automation tools

kp.k: Talent-pool status qualifies the evidence of hiring demand
kp.d: Although the document describes a Legal Engineer role, Halliburton explicitly states that the posting collects talent-pool information for a future related opportunity and is not an application. It therefore documents an employer's specified role and desired capabilities, not a completed hire or confirmed implementation of the described responsibilities.
qs: Please Note: This posting is intended to collect candidate information for Halliburton’s talent pool, and is not considered an application.
By completing the candidate profile, recruiters will have visibility to your information in order to contact you for a future related job opportunity.

cl.s: Concrete claim or prediction about how AI changes legal services, the legal profession, or legal markets (or, for a cross-domain source, its own domain)

pts.k: Halliburton presents AI and automation as means to make its in-house legal services faster, higher-quality and more scalable.
pts.d: The employer describes an AI-enabled legal function under development and assigns the Legal Engineer responsibility for translating legal and business requirements into repeatable technology solutions. Reduced cycle times, minimized risk and improved work quality are intended outcomes, rather than reported results.

pts.k: Halliburton envisages AI-powered workflows, including AI agents, across a broad range of legal and compliance work.
pts.d: The stated scope includes contracts, intake, matter management, regulatory compliance, litigation support, eDiscovery and knowledge management. This is a deployment remit, not evidence that all these applications are already operational. The posting does not specify the agents' autonomy or predict replacement of lawyers.

pts.k: The planned AI-enabled function gives a legal-engineering role responsibility for implementation, adoption, training and governance.
pts.d: Halliburton describes a role combining workflow design, practical generative and agentic AI skills, change management, training and output-validation protocols. A JD is strongly preferred but not required, so the role is not restricted to lawyers. The posting implies professional augmentation and workflow redesign, without specifying who must check particular outputs or authorizing direct reliance on autonomous AI.

cl.s: Evidence basis offered for the claim (data, benchmarks, cases, experience, authority, or none)

pts.k: The evidence is Halliburton's own statement of organizational intent and role requirements; no measured AI benefits are supplied.
pts.d: The careers posting documents the employer's envisaged responsibilities, reporting structure and desired skills. It provides no quantitative results, benchmarks, deployed-system case studies or independent evidence supporting the anticipated speed, quality, risk or cost benefits. Tracking efficiency, accuracy, adoption and savings is a future responsibility, not a report of demonstrated ROI. Repeated copies of the description are not separate evidence. The talent-pool disclaimer also means the posting does not establish that someone has been hired or that an immediate vacancy exists.

cl.s: Stated or implied timeframe, conditions or qualifications under which the claim holds

pts.k: The 2026 posting describes an ongoing transformation and prospective deployments, with no deadline or quantified forecast.
pts.d: The displayed posting date is 07/10/2026. The present-tense description of a department 'shaping' an AI-enabled function is paired with future role responsibilities and a disclaimer referring to future related job opportunities. Implementation is framed as requiring workflow discovery, piloting, readiness assessment, phased rollout, training, post-launch review and compliance with evolving regulation and company policy. No schedule for achieving the expected gains is stated.

cl.s: Who is affected and how (market segment, role, firm type, clients, or the public)

pts.k: The primary affected group is Halliburton's buyer-side legal function and its internal business clients, supported by a specialist legal engineer.
pts.d: In-house lawyers, legal and compliance professionals and staff would receive redesigned workflows and technology training. Business stakeholders and internal clients are intended beneficiaries of faster, higher-quality services. The Legal Engineer would configure and integrate tools and support adoption across teams and geographies, while working onsite in Houston. Private-practice lawyers are identified as collaborators, but the source makes no claim about effects on law-firm staffing, fees, external spend or the wider legal market.
